1) there are no externally validated, well calibrated, and discriminative risk prediction models for frail, older adults with advanced chronic kidney disease, and 2) we need to develop and externally validate risk prediction models that can be used to inform shared decision making and care planning in this population.

there are few reliable, externally validated models that predict the risk of progression of chronic kidney in frail elderly patients, and that there is a need for more models to be externally validated.

the development, validation and application of risk prediction models for the elderly with advanced chronic kidney disease.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the current state-of-the-art in risk prediction for progression to end-stage renal disease and mortality in elderly patients with or without chronic renal disease is insufficient to support shared decision-making and care planning for these patients.

there is a need for a simple risk prediction model that includes a limited number of easily measurable variables, is externally validated in frail elderly, and can be used for shared decision making and care planning for elderly with advanced chronic kidney disease.
, in the absence of a well-validated model, physicians should use their best clinical judgement to inform their patients of the available options, and facilitate a shared decision making process.
